title: GitHub Actions publish workflows: concurrency group must be keyed on the shared release resource, never github.run_id
answers: Why do two release image pushes for the same MLflow version run at the same time?
Why did a manual release label update not wait for an earlier run?
Where is the concurrency key for the push-images or update-release-labels workflow defined?
How do I make a new publish workflow serialize per release tag?
body:
Path: .github/workflows/push-images.yml (release image pushes on release events) and .github/workflows/update-release-labels.yml (release label updates, manual dispatch with a release tag input) set the top-level `concurrency:` block that decides which runs queue behind each other.
Rule: Key the group on the thing being published, e.g. `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}` for image pushes and `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.release.tag_name || github.ref }}` for label updates (falls back to ref for manual runs). `github.run_id` is unique per run, so it serializes nothing.
Symptom: Two runs for the same release could execute concurrently, racing on the same images or labels and leaving partial state.
Constraints: Keep `cancel-in-progress: false` for publish workflows so an in-flight publish completes. Remember GitHub keeps only one pending run per group, so a third run can displace a queued one; the key only controls ordering, not delivery.
applies: Applies to MLflow GitHub Actions workflows that publish release artifacts or labels; does not cover PR test workflows that should cancel superseded runs.
says: Two release image pushes for the same MLflow version run at the same time and race each other
A manual release label update did not wait for an earlier label run to finish
Where is the concurrency group set for the release image push or release label update workflows?
How should a new publish workflow queue runs per release tag so they do not overlap?
search: GitHub Actions publish workflows concurrency key: release image push and release label update workflows must group runs by the release tag, not the run id, so same-release publishes serialize. Keep cancel-in-progress false for publishing; grouping only controls ordering and does not guarantee delivery of queued runs.
